description: The runtime channels between cloud, agent and root (ADR-048 DEC-2, DEC-4.12, DEC-5.7, DEC-5.8, DEC-5.14, DEC-9, DEC-10, DEC-23, DEC-27): the MQTT topics, the activation API, the hand-off commands with which the agent carries cloud-signed statements to root, the update channel root consumes, and the result telemetry that reports what root did. delivery.json is the provisioning delivery and its USB form; this file is everything that happens after the device is provisioned. The agent is a carrier on all of these: it checks the form of what it carries, never the meaning, and root verifies every statement itself (statements.json verified_by).

mqtt.transport: TLS on 8883 only; the broker is named by the signed site config, never by an activation response (DEC-10.1).
mqtt.device_identifier: device_id is the device UUID of the signed manifest. The ACL also admits the MQTT client id and the device code as the device level for devices that predate the UUID names, and the HMI watch stream is named by the device code; a topic of this contract always names the UUID.

commands.writer: The cloud's one command publisher, which signs a platform-actor command envelope for a Suderra OS device (DEC-9.2); the broker ACL lets no other principal write a command topic (DEC-9.3).

activation.description: How a provisioned device obtains its per-device MQTT credentials and has the cloud commit the activation (DEC-5.7). The cloud answers with credentials, root later accepts the activation receipt the cloud issues after the device's first authenticated CONNECT (handoff.commands.activation_receipt).

endpoint.base_url: The https base URL of /etc/suderra/cloud-endpoint in the signed OS image: the same endpoint root fetches the provisioning delivery from.

activation.endpoint_rule: Root's provisioning fetch and the agent's activation reach the cloud only through a port both device rulesets let out: https on tcp 443, with the endpoint URL carrying no port or port 443. An image whose cloud-endpoint names another port fails its build check (Suderra-OS tests/image-contracts/board-file-contract-test.sh), because nothing on the device can reach it. Every URL a signed update statement names is held to the same reach (update_channel.fetch).
activation.endpoint_source: The endpoint comes from the signed OS image (/etc/suderra/cloud-endpoint, one https base URL line, mutable-state.json image_files). Neither the provisioning manifest, an activation response nor the technician sets it, so a hostile delivery cannot redirect the device.

token.rule: The cloud issues a provisioning manifest for a Suderra OS device only under a provisioning token issued at most 4 hours earlier (DEC-5.12); a token older than that is refused like any other refusal. The generic channel keeps its own, longer, token lifetime. The token is single-use and bound to the device binding of the manifest reservation until the activation commits (DEC-5.7).

activation.binding_rule: The activation request MUST carry deviceBinding, the hardware binding root recorded (schemas/edge-activation-request.schema.json requires it), and the cloud MUST refuse, without committing the activation or issuing credentials, an activation whose binding differs from the one the manifest reservation was made for. The request MAY carry installedManifest, the statement digest of the manifest root installed: when present it is the digest the receipt names, and the cloud MUST refuse one that is not a manifest it issued to this device; when absent the receipt names the manifest the cloud issued last.

self_register.rule: A Suderra OS device never self-registers with a tenant token (DEC-5.12): the Suderra OS agent has no self-registration path compiled in, and the cloud's self-register endpoint creates only generic-channel device rows, which receive no Suderra OS manifest, no signed command and no hand-over statement.

activation.commit: The activation commits when the device's own credentials first authenticate an MQTT CONNECT (DEC-5.7); only then does the cloud issue the activation receipt.

handoff.description: Hand-off commands: the cloud's way to give root a signed statement it can only reach through the agent. The agent carries the statement from the command plane into a file root reads and does nothing else; root verifies it itself and records the outcome (DEC-5.8, DEC-5.14, DEC-2.3). Nothing the agent writes is evidence of anything: a statement it wrote without verification fails at root.

envelope.family: The agent's signed command envelope (sens-api-gateway src/command_envelope), signed by the platform actor's command-purpose key, which the trust-anchors bundle anchors and the RBAC manifest maps to the platform actor (DEC-9.1, DEC-9.4).
envelope.iat_rule: The agent accepts an envelope whose iat is at most 60 seconds ahead of its own clock (MAX_IAT_CLOCK_SKEW_SECS) and refuses one whose iat lies further ahead; this is the only skew the contract allows (DEC-7.5).
envelope.param_rule: Command parameters are flat strings and integers: an envelope cannot sign a nested object (SENSOR-HIGH-209), which is why a statement travels as one string.

statement_param.name: statement
statement_param.rule: A string holding the DSSE envelope JSON exactly as the cloud produced and stored it. The agent writes those bytes verbatim and re-serializes nothing, because re-serializing would silently repair an envelope root must refuse (a duplicate member) and change the bytes the cloud recorded.

handoff.authorization: The commands need no RBAC role. The envelope's signature must verify against an RBAC-manifest actor key (the bundle's platform command key), and an unsigned envelope is refused in Enforcing mode, which is the only mode a Suderra OS agent has. The statement itself is signed separately by its own purpose key (statements.json), so a stolen command key alone can deliver only statements that were validly signed, each of which root accepts at most once and only inside its window. A dedicated permission granted only to the platform actor would be stricter; it needs a new member of the agent's Permission enum and of the RBAC schema's permission vocabulary, and belongs to the DEC-9 hardening of P2.

activation_receipt.agent_checks: Size, DSSE envelope form, payloadType, and every check of the receipt except the ones statements.json assigns to root alone (verified_by.agent), against the edge-provisioning key pinned in the OS image: every edge-provisioning anchor of the bundle is that pin (anchor-not-os-pinned), so the pin and the bundle's anchor are one key.

lifecycle_request.agent_checks: Size, DSSE envelope form and payloadType only: the device-lifecycle key is pinned in the OS image alone, so the agent is not a verifier of this statement.

request_update.agent_checks: Size, DSSE envelope form and a payloadType of one of the carried statements; nothing else, and the spool bounds of update_channel.spool.
request_update.cloud_producer: apps/sensor-service/src/edge-device/edge-update-manifest.service.ts (new in P1; edge-update, os-update), site-config-manifest.service.ts (site-config, site-netpolicy) and trust-anchor-bundle.service.ts (trust-anchors), delivered by the same hand-over service as the other two commands

response.rule: Every hand-off command is answered on the response topic, accepted or refused: result.handed_to_root says whether the statement is now a file root reads, statement_digest names it, and reasons says why not. A refused command writes nothing.

handoff.delivery_rule: At-least-once, until settled. The cloud keeps each statement it owes a device and publishes it again, at most once per redelivery interval, on every heartbeat that finds it unsettled, because a non-retained publish to an offline device is lost; it settles a statement when the agent's response names its digest with handed_to_root true. The agent's handling is idempotent: the same statement is the same file. For request_update a hand-over only means the spool holds the file, so the cloud treats the request as concluded only by a result document (result_telemetry) that names the statement digest, and stops redelivering at the statement's expires_at.

update_channel.description: What root consumes: signed statements the agent wrote into its update-request spool, or, from P3, that a USB ingress copied there (DEC-2.3, DEC-2.9, DEC-2.11, DEC-4.12). Root treats a spool entry as hostile input: it verifies the statement against the keys pinned in the OS image or, for site-config and site-netpolicy, the verified bundle, applies its own sequence and rollback floors, and installs through the one installer.

spool.entry: One DSSE envelope of one carried statement, exactly the bytes the cloud produced: no wrapper document, no re-serialization. What root needs beyond the statement comes from signed members of the statement (fetch below), never from the entry.
spool.name: <statement digest>.dsse: the 64 lowercase hex of the statement digest (statements.json dsse.statement_digest), so a repeated request replaces itself.
spool.temporary_rule: The agent writes <temporary name>, fsyncs it and file and directory, then rename(2)s it to its name; the temporary name is a dot-file, so root never reads one. The agent removes a temporary file another process left behind before it counts the directory.
spool.backlog_rule: A request that would exceed max_pending_entries or max_pending_bytes is refused (update-requests-backlog) and nothing is written; a request for a statement already in the directory replaces it and is never counted twice.
spool.agent_is_only_writer: Root never writes, renames or deletes inside the spool (DEC-4.3). The agent removes an entry once /run/suderra/results holds a result, of any outcome, whose subject.statement_digest is the entry's name (the request is then concluded: update_channel.settlement), and any entry older than max_entry_age_seconds.
spool.trigger: suderra-edge-request.path watches the directory and starts suderra-edge-request.service, which consumes one entry at a time under /run/suderra-update.lock, shared with the RAUC processes (DEC-2.3, DEC-2.9).
spool.root_reads: A name that is not name_pattern is ignored. Root opens an entry with openat(O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK) and refuses anything that is not a regular file (symlink, FIFO, device, directory) or larger than max_entry_bytes by fstat on the open descriptor (request-not-regular-file, request-too-large). It then copies at most max_entry_bytes + 1 bytes into its own root-only directory and refuses the entry with request-too-large when the copy is longer than max_entry_bytes, because the agent is the spool's writer and can grow the file through its own descriptor after the fstat. Root processes only the copy.
spool.concluded: Root concludes every entry with exactly one result document that names the statement digest (update_channel.settlement) and records the digest under /data/suderra/os/requests/. It skips a concluded entry silently, so an entry that stays in the spool until the agent prunes it never produces a second result. A conclusion is final: a refusal is never reconsidered, and the same intent reaches root again only as a new statement with a new digest.

fetch.rule: Every URL a carried statement names (release_statement.url, artifact_url, bundle.url, site_bundle_url) is common.schema.json fetch_url: https on port 443 (no port, or :443), a lowercase DNS name whose last label starts with a letter, so never an IP literal, and no userinfo. Root fetches only from the signed URL, follows no redirect to another host, and aborts a transfer that exceeds the byte bound below with the result reason fetch-failed. The host is the platform's artifact host, the one the root installer's egress set of the device firewall names (DEC-11.4, DEC-11.5): a host outside that set is unreachable, so the cloud signs only URLs of that host.
fetch.artifact_bound: The release artifact is read at most as many bytes as the signed release statement's artifact.size_bytes and the RAUC bundle at most bundle.size_bytes; both are signed, so no URL can make root read more.

fetch: release_statement.url: the suderra.edge-release.v1 envelope, at most update_channel.fetch.max_release_statement_bytes, whose statement digest must equal release_statement.digest
artifact_url: the release artifact, whose size and sha256 and whose suderra-agent member's digest come from the release statement (DEC-1.5)
suderra.edge-update.v1.root_action: Installs the release through the one installer (suderra-installer edge update): verify, download, check, unpack beside the current release, switch current atomically, restart the agent, run the health window; a failed window restores the previous release and the site config version it ran with together (DEC-2.6, EI-055).
suderra.edge-update.v1.maintenance: The statement's own local_approval and max_outage_seconds, and the acceptance window.

fetch: bundle.url: the RAUC bundle, whose size and sha256 must equal bundle.size_bytes and bundle.digest; root installs from the verified copy it holds, never by re-reading a path
suderra.os-update.v1.root_action: Runs the preflight (compatible, min_current_version, rollback floor, supported_agent_abi against the installed agent), hands the verified bundle to suderra-ota, which installs it into the inactive slot through RAUC, schedules the approved reboot and leaves the new slot on trial until the health gate marks it good; the OS rollback floor rises to rollback_floor only then (DEC-2.5, DEC-2.9, DEC-23).
suderra.os-update.v1.maintenance: The statement's own local_approval and max_outage_seconds, and the acceptance window.

fetch: site_bundle_url: the suderra.site-bundle.v1 document with the site files and the RBAC manifest the site config names by digest, read at most update_channel.fetch.max_site_bundle_bytes; a site-config statement on this channel without it cannot be applied (site-bundle-missing)
suderra.site-config.v1.root_action: Verifies the site config, the RBAC manifest and the files against it, writes the complete new site directory under a temporary name next to the installed one and activates it with rename(2), updates the install receipt, then reloads the agent (ExecReload) when that is enough and restarts it otherwise; a changed revpi/config.rsc is loaded into piControl by root's own tool, never by the agent. A failed health window restores the previous site version (DEC-4.12, DEC-2.6). Refreshing an expiring RBAC manifest is the same path: a new site config at the next update_seq that names the renewed manifest; there is no separate RBAC channel.
suderra.site-config.v1.maintenance: Root requires a local approval, and reports approval-missing if the window closes without one, when the new site config changes io-config.yaml, site-policy.json or revpi/config.rsc compared with the installed one (DEC-4.12, DEC-13.4); a change of config.yaml and the RBAC manifest alone needs only the acceptance window.

suderra.site-netpolicy.v1.root_action: Renders the policy with the typed renderer, runs nft -c against the running kernel, loads it atomically, falls back to the last-known-good ruleset and raises an alarm when the load fails, and installs the statement as site-netpolicy.dsse beside the site config so it is re-verified before every start (DEC-11.7). The policy cannot remove the WAN broker and API rule, because root refuses a policy whose effective interface roles leave the device no wan interface (interface-mapping-invalid), before it renders anything.
suderra.site-netpolicy.v1.maintenance: The acceptance window; a policy that changes the OT allowlist needs no local approval and no blockers check, because it can only narrow or widen what the agent reaches, the interface mapping check keeps a wan interface, and nft's atomic load keeps the previous rules on failure.

suderra.trust-anchors.v1.root_action: Verifies the bundle against the fleet-root key pinned in the OS image, applies the bundle_seq ratchet (a smaller bundle_seq is refused, an equal one only for the identical bundle), checks that the device's tenant is in tenant_scope and that every edge-release and edge-provisioning anchor is an OS-pinned key, and installs it as trust-anchors.dsse (DEC-3.7, DEC-22).
suderra.trust-anchors.v1.maintenance: The bundle carries no window of its own; root accepts it at any time and the agent re-verifies it when it next loads it.

maintenance.window: The acceptance window of a statement, not_before <= now < expires_at, is the maintenance window the cloud chose. Root verifies an edge-update, an os-update, a site-config and a site-netpolicy only inside it and concludes an entry outside it at its first look, with not-yet-valid or expired (update_channel.settlement). Root never holds a statement for its window to open: the cloud delivers only inside the window (settlement.delivery_window).

blockers.rule: Root refuses to start an edge-update, an os-update or a site-config while the agent holds an active alarm or a forced output value (DEC-13.4); the result reason is maintenance-blocked. Only a running control loop can hold either, so the gate blocks only while the agent unit is in one of agent_unit.blocking_active_states. In any other unit state (inactive, failed, activating, deactivating) the agent has no alarm or forced value to protect, because its outputs are held in their safe state (DEC-6.3, DEC-13.1), so an absent, stale or unreadable health view never blocks, and the update that repairs or replaces a broken agent can always start. While the unit is active, an update_blockers list that is not empty blocks, and so does an unavailable health view (absent, unreadable, larger than 64 KiB, missing or ill-formed in a member root reads, or stale), because an agent that runs and says nothing cannot prove that no alarm is active. Bounded by construction: the unit leaves the active state when its watchdog fires, and an operator can sign the override below.

health_view.read_rule: For this gate root reads three members: schema must be suderra.agent-health.v1, update_blockers a duplicate-free list of known blockers and updated_at a valid instant; a view that fails any of them is unavailable. The other members are the health gate's business (DEC-6.8) and never make this gate refuse.
health_view.freshness_rule: While it runs on Suderra OS the agent rewrites the document at least every refresh_seconds, also when nothing changed, because a view written only on change cannot prove it is current; a view whose updated_at is more than max_age_seconds away from root's clock, in either direction, is stale.

blockers.recheck: Root evaluates the gate before it fetches anything and again at the moment it would stop the agent or schedule the reboot, because a local approval can take until the end of the window and an alarm can start meanwhile.

override.rule: An edge-update or os-update with blockers_override true, which the schema allows only together with local_approval true, ignores the gate: root applies it after the local approval whatever update_blockers holds and whether the view is available. The cloud signs it only on an operator's explicit request, and the local approval means a person on site has seen the alarm or the forced value. It is the way out when a hostile agent keeps update_blockers non-empty or a stale view alive, and an edge-update with it replaces and restarts that agent. A site-config has no override: the agent is replaced by an edge-update first.

maintenance.local_approval: A statement with local_approval true is applied only after a local operator approval, a root-local action whose mechanism the OS owns; root waits for it at most until the statement's expires_at and without one by then concludes with the result reason approval-missing.
maintenance.outage_budget: max_outage_seconds bounds the outage of one update, from the shutdown safe-state to the first control tick; the health window of the update fails when the budget is exceeded.
maintenance.after_failure: After a rollback root takes no further update from the spool until a new statement with a larger update_seq arrives: a rollback never loops (DEC-2 risks).

settlement.description: How a request ends and what the cloud does about it. A request ends with exactly one result document that names its statement digest, and root's handling of a digest is final, so a refusal is final for that statement whatever its reason: root never defers a statement for its window to open, a blocker to clear or a clock to sync. The agent removes the spool entry when it sees that result and the cloud stops redelivering the statement when it sees it; both read the same document, so they agree by construction (fixtures/update-channel/settlement-vectors.json). What differs between refusals is whether the cloud may issue the same intent again, and it always does so as a new statement.
settlement.settled_by: A result document of the request's result kind whose subject.statement_digest is the statement's digest, with any outcome (ok, rejected, failed, alarm). Nothing else settles a request: not the hand-over response, which says only that the spool holds the file, not the agent's removal of the entry, and not silence, which ends at the statement's expires_at, when the cloud marks the request lapsed.

delivery_window.rule: The cloud delivers a statement that has a window only inside it and with at least delivery_margin_seconds left, not_before <= now < expires_at - delivery_margin_seconds on the cloud's clock, and issues windows no longer than spool.max_entry_age_seconds, because the agent prunes an older entry. It never delivers early to have root hold the statement.

class_rules.retryable: The cause is outside the statement and may clear (the clock, the network, the agent's alarms, a filesystem step): the cloud may issue the intent again without an operator, bounded by reissue.
class_rules.reschedule: The window passed without the update being applied (it closed before root looked, or no operator approved on site): the cloud marks the request lapsed, tells the operator, and issues a new statement only when an operator chooses a new window.
class_rules.final: The statement, the artifact or the device state is the cause: refused statements are forged, replayed, for another device, below a floor or malformed, and an installation or load that failed would fail the same way again. The cloud marks the request failed and alerts; recovery is a different statement (another release, bundle or policy) after the cause is fixed.

reissue.rule: A re-issue is a new statement of the same kind and intent, never the same bytes: a not_before later than the refused statement's own makes its digest new, and its update_seq is greater than every update_seq the cloud has issued to the device for that kind, because root spends a sequence value when it has verified a statement (statements.json sequences.spending), so the value of a refused statement is gone. The cloud issues the next one at the earliest min_interval_seconds after the result, and stops campaign_max_seconds after the first statement of the intent, when it marks the request failed and alerts.

settlement.approvals_note: A retryable refusal costs a new statement, so the planned suderra.edge-update.v2 must bind its approvals to the device and the release, not to one statement digest, or every maintenance-blocked refusal would need a new two-person approval (statements.json planned_successors).

time.description: Which clock state each consumer needs (ADR-048 DEC-7). The state is the one root's time helper writes to /run/suderra/time-state (schemas/time-state.schema.json): unsynced, synced-unauthenticated or synced-nts. synced-unauthenticated exists only because the signed site policy (config-integrity key) explicitly marked a plain NTP source (DEC-7.1); no policy, and the default sources are NTS only, so before a policy is installed the only synced state is synced-nts. The device-lifecycle and edge-activation-receipt statements are windowed too but belong to their own hand-over units (handoff.commands), whose result kinds define no clock reason; their clock rule is not part of this table.
time.stale_rule: The root helper rewrites the document at least every refresh_seconds. A reader treats an absent, unreadable or non-conforming document, and one whose updated_at is more than max_age_seconds away from its own clock in either direction, as unsynced.

root-acceptance.rule: Root evaluates the window of a statement, not_before <= now < expires_at, only against a synchronized clock, and concludes with clock-unsynced, before it verifies the statement and spending nothing, when the state is unsynced. synced-unauthenticated suffices because only a signed site policy produces it (DEC-7: the signed exception for a site that cannot reach an NTS server) and the time floor (DEC-7.2) bounds any rewind; an installation that must not trust a plain NTP source does not mark one.

agent-fresh-actuation.rule: Actuation that depends on freshness (a command envelope's iat and exp) is held or refused with the retryable result clock-unsynced while the state is unsynced; the check is never skipped (DEC-7.5).

agent-local-control.rule: Local control, safe-state and alarms never depend on time and run in every state; the agent does not exit because the clock is unsynced (DEC-7.5).

result_telemetry.description: How the typed results root writes reach the cloud (DEC-27). Root writes suderra.result.v1 documents; the agent publishes them; the cloud stores them per device as device-reported evidence, never as authority.
result_telemetry.source: /run/suderra/results, written by root (mutable-state.json): one JSON document per result, schemas/result.schema.json.
result_telemetry.file_name_rule: <seq, 16 digits>-<kind>.json, with the prefix volatile- while /data is not available, so the result exists only in /run until /data is back (Suderra-OS src/results.rs).
result_telemetry.payload: Exactly one suderra.result.v1 document per message, byte for byte the document root wrote: the agent parses it only to check that it is a result document and republishes the bytes it read.
result_telemetry.publication_rule: The agent publishes every result of the directory in seq order once per MQTT session and again after a reconnect until the broker acknowledged it, and keeps the highest acknowledged seq in $DATA/state. The cloud deduplicates on (device_id, seq); seq is monotonic per device and assigned by root.
result_telemetry.acl: A device publishes only on its own results topic; the cloud's result consumer subscribes with a tenant-scoped service grant (mqtt-auth.service.ts checkTopicAccess).
result_telemetry.trust: Unsigned observation: results are never authority (DEC-27); the cloud records them as device-reported evidence.
